gates.question: Does the solvent step you describe fall within the affected source definition (i.e., is it part of the collection of coating operations, storage, mixing, conveyance, or waste handling used for surface coating of plastic parts)?

gates.quote: The affected source is the collection of all of the items listed in paragraphs (b)(1) through (4) of this section that are used for surface coating of plastic parts and products within each subcategory.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Coal- and Oil-Fired Electric Utility Steam Generating Units

gates.question: Is the unit a coal-fired EGU or an oil-fired EGU as defined in § 63.10042?
gates.test: yes -> unit is the category (coal- or oil-fired EGU) that this subpart addresses; no -> unit is not that category and this subpart does not apply
gates.quote: You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate a coal-fired EGU or an oil-fired EGU as defined in § 63.10042 of this subpart.

gates.question: Is the unit located within a contiguous area and under common control with other coal- or oil-fired EGUs at the same site (i.e., part of the collection of EGUs that forms the affected source)?
gates.test: yes -> the unit is part of the affected source collection of EGUs at that site; no -> the unit would be considered individually as an affected EGU if it otherwise meets the definitions
gates.quote: This subpart applies to each individual or group of two or more new, reconstructed, or existing affected source(s) as described in paragraphs (a)(1) and (2) of this section within a contiguous area and under common control.

gates.question: Does the unit burn oil for more than 10.0 percent of average annual heat input over the prior three calendar years (after the facility compliance date) or more than 15.0 percent in any one year?
gates.test: yes -> unit meets the oil-fired EGU threshold (oil-fired EGU) and may be subject to this subpart; no -> unit does not meet the oil-fired EGU threshold and may be a different EGU type (e.g., natural gas-fired) and thus may be excluded
gates.quote: burns oil for more than 10.0 percent of the average annual heat input during the 3 previous calendar years after the compliance date for your facility in § 63.9984

gates.question: Is the unit a natural gas-fired EGU as defined in § 63.10042 (i.e., not a coal- or oil-fired EGU), such that it would be excluded from this subpart under § 63.9983(b)?
gates.test: yes -> unit is excluded from this subpart per § 63.9983(b); no -> unit is not excluded on that basis and may be subject if other criteria met
gates.quote: Any electric utility steam generating unit that is not a coal- or oil-fired EGU and that meets the definition of a natural gas-fired EGU in § 63.10042.

gates.question: Was the unit constructed (i.e., construction commenced) after May 3, 2011 (i.e., is it new relative to the UUUUU dates)?
gates.test: yes -> unit is a new EGU under this subpart (subject to new-source provisions); no -> unit is existing or reconstructed and is subject as such
gates.quote: An EGU is new if you commence construction of the coal- or oil-fired EGU after May 3, 2011.

candidates.title: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Major Sources: Industrial, Commercial, and Institutional Boilers and Process Heaters

gates.question: Is the unit an industrial, commercial, or institutional boiler or process heater as defined in § 63.7575 located at, or part of, a major source of HAP?
gates.test: yes -> the subpart DDDDD could apply to the boiler at that major source; no -> this subpart does not apply
gates.quote: You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate an industrial, commercial, or institutional boiler or process heater as defined in § 63.7575 that is located at, or is part of, a major source of HAP, except as specified in § 63.7491.

gates.question: Is the affected source the collection at the major source of all existing industrial, commercial, and institutional boilers and process heaters within a subcategory (i.e., is this boiler part of that collection at a major source)?
gates.test: yes -> the boiler is part of the affected-source collection and the subpart's affected-source provisions apply; no -> applicability must be evaluated for the individual boiler
gates.quote: The affected source of this subpart is the collection at a major source of all existing industrial, commercial, and institutional boilers and process heaters within a subcategory as defined in § 63.7575.

gates.question: Is the facility a major source of HAP as defined in § 63.2 (i.e., meets the major-source thresholds applicable to this subpart)?
gates.test: yes -> DDDDD applies to boilers at major sources (subject to other exclusions); no -> DDDDD does not apply because it is limited to major sources (with noted exceptions)
gates.quote: For purposes of this subpart, a major source of HAP is as defined in § 63.2, except that for oil and natural gas production facilities, a major source of HAP is as defined in § 63.7575.

gates.question: Is the unit an electric utility steam generating unit (EGU) covered by subpart UUUUU or a natural gas-fired EGU firing at least 85 percent natural gas on an annual heat input basis (both of which are excluded from DDDDD)?
gates.test: yes -> unit is excluded from DDDDD under § 63.7491(a); no -> unit remains potentially subject to DDDDD if at a major source
gates.quote: An electric utility steam generating unit (EGU) covered by subpart UUUUU of this part or a natural gas-fired EGU as defined in subpart UUUUU of this part firing at least 85 percent natural gas on an annual heat input basis.

gates.question: Was the boiler or process heater constructed after June 4, 2010 (i.e., is it new) or reconstructed after that date?
gates.test: yes -> boiler is 'new' or 'reconstructed' for this subpart and subject to new-source provisions; no -> boiler is existing for this subpart
gates.quote: A boiler or process heater is new if you commence construction of the boiler or process heater after June 4, 2010, and you meet the applicability criteria at the time you commence construction.

Whether the unit is part of the affected-source collection at the major source (contiguous/common control with other boilers/process heaters)
Date of construction or reconstruction relative to June 4, 2010

Confirm whether the facility is a major source of HAP (major-source determination under § 63.2).
Confirm whether the unit is under common control and within a contiguous area with other EGUs or boilers at the site (i.e., part of the same affected source).

candidates.title: Glass Manufacturing (area source)

gates.question: Does the plant manufacture glass (e.g., flat glass, glass containers, or pressed and blown glass) by melting raw materials at the plant site?
gates.test: Yes -> plant falls into the glass manufacturing category (proceed to affected_source); No -> this subpart likely does not apply
gates.quote: A glass manufacturing facility is a plant site that manufactures flat glass, glass containers, or pressed and blown glass by melting a mixture of raw materials

gates.question: Is the source an area source (i.e., does not have the potential to emit any single HAP at ≥9.07 Mg/yr (10 tpy) or more)?
gates.test: Yes -> area-source criteria met (proceed to affected_source); No -> source is major and this area-source subpart does not apply
gates.quote: that does not have the potential to emit any single HAP at a rate of 9.07 megagrams per year (Mg/yr) (10 tons per year (tpy)) or more

gates.question: Do you operate a continuous glass-melting furnace charged with compounds of one or more glass-manufacturing metal HAP and used to produce glass at a rate of at least 45 Mg/yr (50 tpy)?
gates.test: Yes -> the specific affected-furnace criteria are met (subpart may apply); No -> the specific affected-furnace criteria are not met (subpart may not apply)
gates.quote: The furnace is used to produce glass, which contains one or more of the glass manufacturing metal HAP as raw materials, at a rate of at least 45 Mg/yr (50 tpy).

gates.question: Was construction or reconstruction of the affected source commenced on or before September 20, 2007 (i.e., is it an existing source)?
gates.test: Yes -> source would be an existing affected source; No -> source would be a new affected source
gates.quote: An affected source is an existing source if you commenced construction or reconstruction of the affected source on or before September 20, 2007.

missing: Whether frit production counts as the types of "glass" defined for this subpart (e.g., flat, container, pressed/blown), whether the furnace is continuous, the actual production rate (Mg/yr), whether glass raw materials contain glass-manufacturing metal HAP (nickel) as defined in §63.11459

gates.quote: Paints and allied products means materials such as paints, inks, adhesives, stains, varnishes, shellacs, putties, sealers, caulks, and other coatings from raw materials that are intended to be applied to a substrate

gates.question: Does the affected source at the facility process, use, or generate materials containing HAP as part of paints and allied products manufacturing processes?
gates.test: Yes -> affected-source definition for this subpart is met; No -> subpart likely does not apply
gates.quote: The affected source consists of all paints and allied products manufacturing processes that process, use, or generate materials containing HAP at the facility.

gates.question: Is the operation a research and development facility (excluded from this subpart)?
gates.test: Yes -> exempt from this subpart; No -> not exempt on that basis
gates.quote: The standards of this subpart do not apply to research and development facilities, as defined in section 112(c)(7) of the CAA.

gates.quote: Any material that contains compounds of chromium (VI), lead, or nickel in amounts greater than or equal to 0.1 percent by weight

candidates.title: Engine Test Cells and Stands NESHAP

gates.question: Is the engine test cell/stand located at a major source of HAP emissions?
gates.test: yes -> subject to this subpart; no -> not subject to this subpart
gates.quote: You are subject to this subpart if you own or operate an engine test cell/stand that is located at a major source of HAP emissions.

gates.question: Are the units in question engine test cells/stands used for testing uninstalled stationary or uninstalled mobile (motive) engines?
gates.test: yes -> they are an affected source (collection of equipment/activities); no -> not an affected source under this subpart
gates.quote: An affected source is the collection of all equipment and activities associated with engine test cells/stands used for testing uninstalled stationary or uninstalled mobile (motive) engines located at a major source of HAP emissions.

gates.question: Did an area-source affected portion increase emissions or potential to emit such that it became a major source of HAP?
gates.test: yes -> new or reconstructed affected source at a major source must be in compliance; no -> remains area-source status (different obligations)
gates.quote: If your new or reconstructed affected source is located at an area source that increases its emissions or its potential to emit such that it becomes a major source of HAP, your new or reconstructed affected source must be in compliance

gates.question: Did you commence construction or reconstruction on or before May 14, 2002?
gates.test: yes -> affected source is existing; no -> may be new or reconstructed depending on timing
gates.quote: Existing affected source. An affected source is existing if you commenced construction or reconstruction of the affected source on or before May 14, 2002.

gates.question: Are the changes limited to passive measurement and control instrumentation and electronics?
gates.test: yes -> those items are not included in any affected source reconstruction evaluation; no -> those items may be included in reconstruction evaluation
gates.quote: In addition, passive measurement and control instrumentation and electronics are not included as part of any affected source reconstruction evaluation.

gates.question: When did you start up the new or reconstructed affected source (date of initial startup)?
gates.test: start up before May 27, 2003 -> must comply by May 27, 2003; start up on/after May 27, 2003 -> must comply upon startup (with later-specified exceptions/dates)
gates.quote: If you start up your new or reconstructed affected source before May 27, 2003, you must comply with the emission limitations in this subpart no later than May 27, 2003;

missing: Whether the test cells/stands are located at a plant that is a major source (actual or potential HAP tpy)
Dates when each component was replaced or added (to determine commencement and whether before/after May 14, 2002)

Detailed list of replaced/added components to identify which are passive measurement/control instrumentation or air pollution control equipment
Fixed capital cost of the new components and an estimate of cost to construct a comparable new source (to determine the >50% reconstruction threshold)

exemption: Is any portion used exclusively for testing internal combustion engines with rated power less than 25 hp, or exclusively for combustion turbines, rocket engines, noncommercial research/teaching, or testing fuels/transmissions/electronics?

gates.quote: The fixed capital cost of the new components exceeds 50 percent of the fixed capital cost that would be required to construct a comparable new source;

gates.question: Is it technologically and economically feasible for the reconstructed source to meet the relevant standard(s)?
